title: What a Covariate Can and Cannot Buy
scopeNote: This is the covariate-adjustment experiment of the original, narrowed to the one point that changes what a reader is entitled to conclude. The variable-role assignment stage, the whole multivariate half, the homogeneity-of-slopes violation and the described designs to classify stay in the longer version, and the page says so.
summary: A fictional reading programme with a September score as covariate. A real ANCOVA runs on the generated cohort, showing the unadjusted difference, the adjusted difference and the precision each buys. Switching the design between random allocation and two intact classes changes no arithmetic at all, and changes the conclusion completely.
learningObjectives: Read the adjusted difference as the vertical distance between two fitted lines of common slope.
Explain that under randomisation a covariate's main contribution is precision rather than correction.
State what an adjusted difference estimates when the groups were not randomly formed.
Recognise that identical arithmetic can carry entirely different warrants depending on the design.
State the homogeneity-of-regression-slopes assumption and what its failure costs.
interactionTypes: three live controls over the simulated cohort
a real ANCOVA computed on each generated sample
a scatter plot with two fitted lines of common slope and a marked adjusted difference
a design switch that alters the warrant while provably altering no figure
a withheld explanation released after the learner has changed the study
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted. Every cohort is generated and analysed in the browser and is gone when the page is closed.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout. The design switch is a two-option radio group whose labels are both permanently visible, so neither can be truncated and neither state is hidden. The figure carries a description giving both group means on both occasions, the common slope, both differences, both standard errors and the within-group correlation, so no conclusion depends on reading the marks. The two groups differ by marker shape, filled circle against hollow square, and by line dash as well as by colour, and each fitted line is labelled at its right-hand end. The bracket label is drawn with a background-coloured halo so it stays legible over data marks. The figure scrolls sideways rather than shrinking below legible label sizes on a narrow screen, and becomes a keyboard-reachable region when it does. Changes are announced through a polite live region. No timed content and no motion.
dataStatus: Simulated and illustrative. Eighty fictional children, forty per group. The true programme effect is fixed at 6 June points. No figure here is a norm, a real evaluation or a validated benchmark.
simulationNotes: Randomness is seeded with mulberry32 and Box-Muller normals, so a given seed reproduces a cohort exactly. June is generated as a base plus a slope on September plus the fixed effect plus noise, with the slope and residual spread chosen so the within-group correlation matches the covariate-strength control. A genuine ANCOVA is then computed on the generated sample: a pooled within-group slope, an adjusted difference, and standard errors for both the unadjusted and adjusted estimates including the term that penalises adjustment when the group means on the covariate are far apart. The design control is deliberately not passed to either the generator or the analysis; it selects the interpretation paragraph and nothing else, which is the demonstration. Note that the simulation is generous to the intact-classes reading, since September really is the only systematic difference between the groups here; the synthesis says so explicitly, because in real intact groups it never is and that is precisely the difficulty adjustment cannot reach.
readmeTopic: what adjusting for a covariate does to an estimate, and why only the design decides what the estimate means
